records.name: Create and publish course
records.description: Happy-path: Instructor creates a new course from the Courses list, steps through a 5-step guided wizard (title/description, thumbnail, pricing, pricing details, outline method), then builds content (adds resources, video embed, quiz generated by AI), reviews the curriculum in the Setup guide, publishes the course and receives a launch confirmation with the sales link. Entry point: Courses list (logged-in instructor). Exit point: Courses list with the new course marked Published and a visible sales link. Assumes user is logged in with permission to create and publish courses and has files (image, resources) available for upload.
records.problem: User task: Create and publish a new online course so students can purchase and access it. From the user's perspective they expect a guided, linear setup that captures course metadata (title, description, thumbnail), pricing (one-time/payment options), curriculum (outline, lessons, embedded media), and optional AI assistance for outline and quizzes — then publish and get a shareable sales link. From the system perspective the UI enforces a step sequence in a modal wizard for initial metadata, provides upload and preview affordances for images, exposes pricing options and a pricing detail form, offers AI options to generate outlines and quiz questions, surfaces curriculum editing (lesson-level content, resources, quiz blocks), and requires a final publish confirmation. Final result: User-perceived outcome is a published course with curriculum and pricing visible; system-level outcome is a new product record created, curriculum items saved, pricing plan attached, course state changed to Published, and a public sales link generated.
steps: Curriculum — lesson with quiz and resources

records.name: School setup and course creation
records.description: Happy path summary: An authenticated school owner/admin views an empty Students list, is prompted (or redirected) to authorize access to their account, and then lands on the course creation onboarding screen where they can enter a course title/description and use an AI tool to generate an outline. Entry point: logged-in admin dashboard (left navigation visible). Exit point: user has created (or started) a course outline or completed the authorization step. Assumptions: user is signed in with owner/admin privileges; uses a desktop browser; has not yet added students and has not completed email verification (system displays a verify-email banner).
records.problem: User task (user perspective): The user, acting as a school owner or admin, is trying to get their school set up by managing users (students) and beginning course creation. They expect to: 1) see any enrolled students or be able to add/import students; 2) be guided to grant necessary account permissions if required; and 3) start creating a course quickly using an AI outline generator. Interface/system perspective: The UI presents an empty state for Students with primary actions (Add Students, Export CSV, Email Students) and contextual upsell/help; it can surface account-level prompts (email verification banner) and trigger an authorization flow that requests access to profile info. After authorization (or navigation), the system shows a course-creation onboarding form with fields for title and description and a prominent "Generate your outline" action backed by AI tools. Result at the end: User-perceived outcome — the user either granted account access and/or reached the create-course outline screen ready to input content and generate an outline. System-level outcome — the platform records the authorization grant (if approved) and prepares AI-driven course generation using the supplied title/description input.
